# AUDIO PROFILE: Salma
## The Kind Older Sister
Salma is a young Arab woman in her early twenties with a light, warm, distinctly feminine voice. She reads to a sleepy child in a quiet bedroom beside one warm lamp.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: soft, affectionate, reassuring, and natural; never an announcer, never theatrical, never babyish.
Pacing: slow and unhurried at about 53 Arabic words per minute, with a small natural pause at every full stop.
Accent: clear Modern Standard Arabic articulated naturally by an educated Egyptian speaker.
Loudness: constant across all eight files. No escalation, command tone, urgency, fear, sadness, or dramatic climax.
Delivery: speak only the transcript, with no title, page number, instruction, sound effect, or extra words.

lines.style: A gentle welcoming introduction at the story's normal pace. Keep ريم clear and natural. No excitement.

lines.text: قالت أمّها: الألعاب تريد أن تنام.
lines.style: The sentence الألعاب تريد أن تنام is a warm invitation and shared idea, never an instruction, warning, or firm bedtime order. Keep the colon pause natural.

lines.text: فأخذت ريم الدبّ. ووضعته على الرفّ.
lines.style: Two familiar routine steps with one small pause between sentences. Clear shadda in الدبّ and الرفّ, without overemphasis.
This is only a small practical observation. Absolutely no worry, frustration, suspense, sadness, surprise, or rise in loudness.
A simple solution, not a victory. Let ونامت الكرة settle softly after a natural sentence pause.
Give واحدًا واحدًا an evenly spaced, slow, repetitive rhythm like placing two blocks in sequence. No sing-song performance.
Slow gently on هادئة and نائمة. Keep level constant while the energy settles toward stillness.

lines.text: وريم في سريرها. تصبح على خير.
lines.audio_tag: [very slow, drowsy, final, one gentle phrase at a time]
lines.style: This must be the slowest and final delivery in the story. Pause naturally after سريرها. Make تصبح على خير the slowest phrase, settling into silence as a statement, never a question. No extra goodbye or recommendation.
